3990: Osceola County park on Rose Lake near LeRoy, with a swimming beach and boat launch.  Every camper must back in, and generators aren't allowed. --Claude
3992: Missaukee County park on the south side of Crooked Lake, on 60-plus acres with a swimming beach, a paved boat ramp, hiking trails, a modern bathhouse and a rustic cabin.  35 of the sites have electricity; the rest are rustic. --Claude
4002: Alpena County park on Beaver Lake at Lachine, about 22 miles west of Alpena on M-65, with a boat launch. --Claude
4005: Alpena County fairgrounds campground on the Thunder Bay River, run as an ordinary campground rather than for events only; 12 of the sites are along the river. --Claude
4010: Alpena County park on the shore of Long Lake, just off US-23 north of Alpena, with a swimming beach, boat launch and grassy sites, and a nature-study area for hiking. --Claude
4011: Alpena County's largest park, 160 acres on Sunken Lake in Posen Township (Presque Isle County), with a boat launch, swimming, a primitive camping area, and walking trails past sinkholes and a covered bridge. --Claude
4019: Delta County park on 74 acres along the Escanaba River at Gladstone, with a boat launch, disc golf, kayak rentals and five rustic riverside cabins.  21 of the sites have full hookups; the rest have water and electric. --Claude
4021: City of Manistique campground on Lake Michigan, with long, level paved pads, a few primitive tent sites and a boardwalk along the breakwater. --Claude
4027: Kinross Township RV park behind Kinross Community Park, home of the Chippewa County Fairgrounds, half a mile off I-75 exit 378.  52 sites with electric, some with water as well, on grass pads off dirt roads, plus rustic tent sites and a modern bathhouse. --Claude
4029: Forsyth Township park on the Escanaba River in Gwinn, with grassy sites, a beach and a pavilion: 20 full-hookup RV sites, 2 with electric only and 13 primitive tent sites. --Claude
4033: City of Ironwood campground beside the Gogebic County Fairgrounds on US 2, with shaded sites and a small playground.  9 sites have full hookups and the rest electric only. --Claude
4038: Private resort on the Carp River at the foot of Marquette Mountain, about 5 minutes from downtown Marquette, with about 50 full-hookup RV sites, tent sites, 14 cabins, a pool, a hot tub and a bar.  Open all year, but the water and sewer hookups are shut off from late fall to late spring. --Claude
4041: City of Marquette campground on 40 wooded acres fronting the Dead River at the north edge of town, a mile from the Lake Superior beaches, with a sandy beach, two playgrounds, hiking trails, a bike pump track, and links to the city bike path and the Noquemanon trails.  About 100 sites have electric, 38 of them with water and sewer too; the rest are primitive tent sites. --Claude
4064: Private RV park on Hopeville Pond in Griswold, formerly Campers World on Hopeville Pond, open about six months a year.  Seasonal lots, with some sites sold by the night; a pump-out service comes to the sites. --Claude
4141: The Baker River half of Modern America's Riverbrook & Baker River in Rumney, on the river, with a beach for swimming, fishing and tubing.  Riverbrook, its sister campground a mile west on Route 25, has the office, and Campspot books both on one listing.  Open from Memorial Day to Columbus Day, for seasonal campers as well as nightly ones. --Claude
4166: Private family campground on the Mohawk Trail (Route 2) in East Charlemont, in the Berkshires near the Deerfield River, with rental cabins, a snack bar, a game room and a picnic pavilion; seasonal sites as well as nightly ones.  Gravel roads and grass sites; the operator states no RV size limit. --Claude
4184: Private campground on the northwest shore of Moosehead Lake, reached by about 30 miles of improved dirt road (drive carefully, and don't trust GPS).  Some waterfront sites have water and electric, the power from a generator; there is a honey wagon and a bathhouse. --Claude
4189: Family campground with 1,700 feet of Saco River frontage in Brownfield, with sandy-bottomed river swimming, canoe, kayak and tube rentals with a shuttle, and riverside tent sites.  Open May to October, for nightly, weekly and seasonal stays. --Claude
4231: Small family-owned campground in the foothills at Elkin, on the Mountains-to-Sea Trail and near the Yadkin Valley wineries: back-in sites along the creek that runs through it, wide pull-throughs that take big rigs, 4 tent sites, gem mining and a 9-hole disc golf course. --Claude
4236: Small RV resort on 22 acres in Forest City, with concrete pads, a fenced dog park and nature trails; the back-in sites are 35 by 50 feet. --Claude
4249: Small mountain park with about a dozen gravel sites, many of them held by seasonal and full-time campers. --Claude
4250: Small campground on a ridge near Bryson City and the Nantahala, with creekfront sites and room for anything from a van to a big rig. --Claude
4263: Resort on Tranter's Creek west of Washington, with about 3,000 feet of creek frontage, a boat launch, fishing and a pool; big-rig friendly. --Claude
4264: Small RV park on Persimmon Creek, 12 miles west of Murphy, with 19 to 25 sites, some along the creek, and bass and trout ponds. --Claude
4284: Family campground near the North Carolina Zoo in Asheboro, with a playground, gem mining, pedal carts, a dog park, hiking trails, fishing, propane and cabins.  Its website said in October 2026 that the waterslide is closed until further notice. --Claude
